content.markdown:
# Predicting sub-hectare salinity pockets near the Tisa to guide adaptive sampling

## Verified facts
- TloCare uses a 4-ha grid; Tisa-area clients report sunflower failure where maps look good; denser resampling found 0.3–0.8 ha saline pockets the grid skips; denser sampling means more field/lab cost and longer delivery, with service price already pressing the client's acceptability limit. [F1]
- TloCare holds GPS and lab results for ~18,000 points over ten years; client-visible results are pH, phosphorus, potassium, humus and calcification need. [F2]
- Filipović's geostatistical survey found ESP >25% hotspots occupied 18% of the area in micro-depressions, and single-depth sampling underestimated subsurface alkalisation by 30–40%. [F3]
- He mapped ECa with EM38/EM31 across 2,300 ha and produced ECe maps with three salinisation classes covering 8%, 31% and 61% of the area. [F4]
- He trained random forest and gradient boosting classifiers to predict 1-ha parcel reclamation readiness from Sentinel-2, EM38 and soil-map covariates, reaching 79–81% accuracy; misclassified parcels clustered at the solonetz–chernozem transition. [F5]
- SALTMOD was calibrated and validated for solonetz sites in Bečej and Novi Bečej districts. [F6]
- TloCare plans at least one field sensor (electrical conductivity or NIR) in two years for denser coverage without proportional sampling-cost growth; two developers and one GIS specialist can dedicate up to one-third time, with occasional field-team support. [F7]
- Filipović lists openness to joint projects with soil-monitoring-sensor or irrigation-software companies and is cautious about projects requiring >20% administrative time. [F8]

## Our inference
- This suggests a strong method fit: his spatial salinity, EM induction and ML screening work addresses TloCare's need to predict variable zones before sending field teams.
- The cited evidence comes from Bačka and Tamiš–Bega, not the Tisa floodplain parcels named by TloCare, so transfer to 0.3–0.8 ha Tisa pockets must be validated with held-out dense sampling.
- The historical 4-ha grid may be too sparse to label small pockets; his classifiers reached 79–81% accuracy with boundary misclassification; single-depth sampling missed subsurface alkalisation by 30–40%, so surface-only prediction is a risk. His availability is unknown, making collaboration conditional.

## Proposed next steps
- Proposed first experiment (hypothesis): audit analytes and depths in TloCare's ~18,000 records, especially ECe/ESP, and require usable salinity labels. Train a spatial salinity-risk model on non-Tisa parcels, hold out Tisa parcels such as Ravnica Agro near Novi Bečej, compare to the current 4-ha grid baseline, add covariate groups one at a time (Sentinel-2, soil/terrain maps, any EM38/EM31 or field-sensor data), and compare predicted risk zones with denser reference sampling. Measure detection of 0.3–0.8 ha saline pockets and false-alarm rate. Go/no-go after audit and held-out Tisa validation: proceed only if predictions beat baseline on agreed detection and false-alarm criteria and TloCare confirms budget/time for dense sampling; otherwise stop. Researcher proposes model design/validation; company proposes data access, GIS support and, if budget confirmed, dense sampling—not yet committed.
- Draft a data-sharing agreement covering the 18,000 historical GPS/lab records, client parcel boundaries and new validation samples before modelling starts.
- Keep administrative load below the researcher's 20% tolerance and confirm TloCare's one-third developer/GIS capacity in a short written work plan.
- Propose a 12-month timeline (negotiation target): data audit and label check, model development on non-Tisa parcels, held-out Tisa validation over one field season; success is detection rate for 0.3–0.8 ha pockets and false-alarm rate against denser sampling, thresholds agreed before validation.

## Open questions
- Confirm both sides intend a joint project and whether industrial PhD supervision is also of interest; the researcher's industrial PhD willingness and availability are unknown.
- Can TloCare provide a data-sharing agreement covering the 18,000 historical GPS/lab records and client parcel data before work starts?
- Which Tisa-area parcels, such as Ravnica Agro near Novi Bečej, can be densely sampled as validation sites, and what budget and time are available?
- Which field sensor route is planned first, electrical conductivity or near-infrared spectroscopy, and when would it become available?
- What spatial resolution and prediction accuracy must be reached before the workflow guides sampling, and can administration stay below 20% of the researcher's time while confirming one-third developer/GIS capacity?
